      "title": "Fix the invalid conditional terminator in the embed template",

Every embed request that finds an existing topic therefore fails instead of rendering its comments. Replace this with an ordinary `end` and add a test that actually renders the template; the mocked controller tests do not exercise it."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/post.rb",
      "line": 133,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Retain HTML sanitization for raw-HTML posts",
      "body": "This return bypasses sanitization for both creation and subsequent edits. PollFeed supplies external HTML directly, while TopicEmbed appends a source link containing an unescaped URL. For example, an otherwise valid article URL ending in `?x='onclick='alert(1)` injects an event-handler attribute into that link. Nokogiri parsing preserves such attributes, and the resulting cooked HTML is rendered as trusted content in the forum origin. Sanitize the complete raw-HTML output and escape the generated source link."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/topic_embed.rb",
      "line": 48,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Validate import URLs before passing them to Kernel.open",
      "body": "`import_remote` opens its argument before the HTTP URL check in `import`. The Disqus importer calls this method directly with a thread link from the XML export, bypassing TopicRetriever's validation. Ruby's `Kernel.open` interprets a leading pipe as a subprocess, so an export containing a link such as `|id` executes a command as the application user before any URL rejection occurs. Validate the HTTP(S) URI before I/O and use a client without filesystem or subprocess fallback."
    },
    {
      "file": "lib/topic_retriever.rb",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Enforce the host restriction across HTTP redirects",
      "body": "Only the original embed URL is checked here, but `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses open-uri, which automatically follows redirects to other hosts. An allowed-host URL with an open redirect can therefore cause a public embed request to fetch an internal HTTP service or another otherwise-disallowed host, potentially importing its response into a public topic. Validate each redirect destination before following it rather than relying solely on the initial host comparison."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb",
      "line": 35,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Handle feed items without a content element",
      "body": "A valid RSS item can provide its body in `description` or `content:encoded` without a `content` element, and Atom entries can provide only a summary. Calling `scrub` unconditionally on `i.content` raises when that field is absent, aborting the entire poll and preventing later items from being imported. Select the appropriate available body field and handle entries with no body explicitly."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/topic_embed.rb",
      "line": 65,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Resolve relative URLs against the article URI",
      "body": "The prefix concatenation treats protocol-relative URLs as root-relative paths: `//cdn.example.com/image.png` becomes a path on the article's host instead of retaining the CDN host. Path-relative references such as `images/image.png` are left unchanged and subsequently resolve against the forum rather than the original article. Both links and images can therefore break in imported posts. Use URI reference resolution against the article URL for both attributes."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/models/topic_embed.rb",
      "line": 21,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Defer post-creation jobs until the outer import transaction commits",
      "body": "`PostCreator#create` enqueues post-processing and featured-user jobs after its own transaction block, but that transaction joins this outer `Topic.transaction`. Consequently those jobs are published before the imported post and topic are committed, and are also published if the subsequent TopicEmbed insertion fails. A worker can see missing records and skip or fail processing. Preserve the atomic import while deferring these jobs and publication side effects until the outer transaction commits."
    },
    {
      "file": "lib/tasks/disqus.thor",
      "line": 148,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Preserve the original thread creation time during Disqus import",
      "body": "The previous PostCreator call supplied the exported thread's `created_at`, but the replacement passes only its title, and TopicEmbed does not forward a creation timestamp. Imported first posts are now dated at import time while their replies retain their historical dates. This loses original chronology and can place replies before the apparent start of their discussion. Extend the import helper to accept and preserve the exported timestamp."
    },
    {
      "file": "app/assets/javascripts/embed.js",
      "line": 17,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Compare postMessage origins exactly",
      "body": "Substring matching does not establish that a message came from the Discourse origin. For example, `https://forum.example.co` passes this check when discourseUrl is `https://forum.example.com/`. Another window with a reference to the embedding page can therefore send resize messages that hide the comments or disrupt the page layout. Compare against the parsed, exact Discourse origin and verify that the message source is the embedded iframe."
    }
  ]

findings.title: Fix the invalid conditional terminator in the embed template
findings.body: `<%- end if %>` contains an `if` without a condition and produces invalid Ruby when the template is compiled. Every embed request that finds an existing topic therefore fails instead of rendering its comments. Replace this with an ordinary `end` and add a test that actually renders the template; the mocked controller tests do not exercise it.

findings.title: Retain HTML sanitization for raw-HTML posts
findings.body: This return bypasses sanitization for both creation and subsequent edits. PollFeed supplies external HTML directly, while TopicEmbed appends a source link containing an unescaped URL. For example, an otherwise valid article URL ending in `?x='onclick='alert(1)` injects an event-handler attribute into that link. Nokogiri parsing preserves such attributes, and the resulting cooked HTML is rendered as trusted content in the forum origin. Sanitize the complete raw-HTML output and escape the generated source link.

findings.title: Validate import URLs before passing them to Kernel.open
findings.body: `import_remote` opens its argument before the HTTP URL check in `import`. The Disqus importer calls this method directly with a thread link from the XML export, bypassing TopicRetriever's validation. Ruby's `Kernel.open` interprets a leading pipe as a subprocess, so an export containing a link such as `|id` executes a command as the application user before any URL rejection occurs. Validate the HTTP(S) URI before I/O and use a client without filesystem or subprocess fallback.

findings.title: Enforce the host restriction across HTTP redirects
findings.body: Only the original embed URL is checked here, but `TopicEmbed.import_remote` uses open-uri, which automatically follows redirects to other hosts. An allowed-host URL with an open redirect can therefore cause a public embed request to fetch an internal HTTP service or another otherwise-disallowed host, potentially importing its response into a public topic. Validate each redirect destination before following it rather than relying solely on the initial host comparison.

findings.title: Handle feed items without a content element
findings.body: A valid RSS item can provide its body in `description` or `content:encoded` without a `content` element, and Atom entries can provide only a summary. Calling `scrub` unconditionally on `i.content` raises when that field is absent, aborting the entire poll and preventing later items from being imported. Select the appropriate available body field and handle entries with no body explicitly.

findings.title: Resolve relative URLs against the article URI
findings.body: The prefix concatenation treats protocol-relative URLs as root-relative paths: `//cdn.example.com/image.png` becomes a path on the article's host instead of retaining the CDN host. Path-relative references such as `images/image.png` are left unchanged and subsequently resolve against the forum rather than the original article. Both links and images can therefore break in imported posts. Use URI reference resolution against the article URL for both attributes.

findings.title: Defer post-creation jobs until the outer import transaction commits
findings.body: `PostCreator#create` enqueues post-processing and featured-user jobs after its own transaction block, but that transaction joins this outer `Topic.transaction`. Consequently those jobs are published before the imported post and topic are committed, and are also published if the subsequent TopicEmbed insertion fails. A worker can see missing records and skip or fail processing. Preserve the atomic import while deferring these jobs and publication side effects until the outer transaction commits.

findings.title: Preserve the original thread creation time during Disqus import
findings.body: The previous PostCreator call supplied the exported thread's `created_at`, but the replacement passes only its title, and TopicEmbed does not forward a creation timestamp. Imported first posts are now dated at import time while their replies retain their historical dates. This loses original chronology and can place replies before the apparent start of their discussion. Extend the import helper to accept and preserve the exported timestamp.

findings.title: Compare postMessage origins exactly
findings.body: Substring matching does not establish that a message came from the Discourse origin. For example, `https://forum.example.co` passes this check when discourseUrl is `https://forum.example.com/`. Another window with a reference to the embedding page can therefore send resize messages that hide the comments or disrupt the page layout. Compare against the parsed, exact Discourse origin and verify that the message source is the embedded iframe.
